The javadoc in all generated Coalesce evaluator files (and the template) says:
> `This class is generated. Edit {@code X-InEvaluator.java.st} instead.`
The actual template file is `X-CoalesceEvaluator.java.st`. This is a copy-paste error from the `In` evaluator template that will misdirect anyone trying to fix a bug in the generated code.

The `default` branch throws `new IllegalArgumentException()` without including the `elementType` value. Since this is a test that iterates over multiple element types, including the offending type in the message would make failures much easier to diagnose:
```java
default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported element type: " + elementType);
```

These add `import org.apache.lucene.util.BytesRef;` to non-BytesRef builders (Boolean, Double, Float, Int, Long). The import is only needed for the `{@link BytesRef}` reference in the javadoc of the new `copyFrom` method. While technically it makes the javadoc link resolve, it's misleading to import `BytesRef` in a `BooleanBlockBuilder` or `DoubleBlockBuilder`. The template (#N1GR0) places this import in the `$else$` branch unconditionally. Consider using the fully-qualified name in the javadoc instead, or making the javadoc text type-conditional.
